Stellenbosch Student Attacks

By: Catherine Rice | Commission

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
The university town of Stellenbosch is known for it's beauty and relative safety, but an alarming crime trend has struck fear into the hearts of students living there.

Unique Selling Point:
In the past four months, there have been five incidents of abductions involving students from the University of Stellenbosch. In June, a girl was abducted outside a nightclub in the early hours of the morning, and released unharmed after being driven around. In the same month, a student couple who had stopped to star gaze on the Franschoek Pass, was abducted and taken to an abandoned house where their parents were phoned and a ransom demanded. Both parents paid, and the couple was released unharmed. In August, a student was abducted and released 9kms outside of Stellenbosch, after being robbed of his cellphone and money. In a recent incident on the 8th of September, a university student was abducted outside a nightclub and driven around for several hours. He was robbed of his valuables and eventually released unharmed in Cloetesville, in the early hours of the morning. In the most recent case, on the 3rd of October, a 20 year old Stellenbosch University student was walking home in the early hours of the morning when she was abducted and held for ransom. Once her family paid, she was released the following day. The alleged kidnappers, two Zimbabwean nationals, were arrested, and face charges of kidnapping, extortion, rape and contravening the Immigration Act. They will apply for bail on the 23rd of October in the Stellenbosch Magistrate's Court.

Summary:
Crime in the once relatively safe university town of Stellenbosch has spiked in recent months. Students reporting incidents of violent muggings has become a daily occurrence. On September 18th, a first year student was walking to the engineering faculty just 500 meters from his home when he was held up at gunpoint in the morning. His backpack was stolen and the two attackers fled on foot. Most concerning are the abductions. Parents of students are so concerned they have created safety WhatsApp groups and are urging students to sign up to private security companies.

Script:


NATSOUND (Cellphone footage) “Guys they went slow, why did they go slow. This is when you run guys. This is not okay”.

VOXPOP With Stellenbosch you don’t expect it. You’re lulled into a false sense of security.

NATSOUND (Cellphone footage) “The car’s looking for us. Run. Run.”

VOXPOP I came to Stellenbosch thinking you know its very safe, look at the buildings it’s stunning. Nothing could go wrong.

NATSOUND (Cellphone footage) “We’re almost there. Run, run”

VOXPOP After a couple of really traumatic experiences, I realized it’s very much still South Africa. We need to be safe. We need to be cautious.

NATSOUND (Cellphone footage) “Hide”.

CUT TO BLACK

VO 1 Stellenbosch - a beautiful university town with oak shaded streets and Cape Dutch architecture.

VO 2 But beneath it’s charming surface, a darkness has emerged. There’s been a disturbing rise in crimes - targetting students. In the worst cases, some are even kidnapped.

VO 3 Since June, there have been five abduction cases.

UPSOUND Mother: I was asleep so when the phone rang it didn’t initially register. 06:21 But, when I heard her sobbing that’s when it kicked in and my heart was in my mouth. As a mother, I felt absolutely helpless.

VO 4 The mother agreed to talk to us if we hid her identity. Her daughter, who graduated last year, had returned for a night out with friends in June and was walking from one nightclub to another when she was abducted.

UPSOUND Mother: How it happened is unclear, but having spoken to her friends who said she disappeared from next to them as if she disappeared into thin air. 03:23 Because it was a crowd, they look and watch who are friends and they come between them, you don’t notice. They’ve obviously all had a few drinks 04:02 She was edged out and there was a car waiting there and she was put into a car.

VO 5 Her daughter was driven around and ordered to hand over her phone.

UPSOUND Mother: By the grace of God she was dropped off not too far from where this happened she was dropped off in the built up area of Stellenbosch.

VO 6 Miraculously she was unharmed, but this would foreshadow a far more serious case, that happened exactly one week later.

VO 7 Two first year Stellenbosch university students - headed to the nearby Franschoek Pass to stargaze.

UPSOUND Father: My wife tried to contact my son at about 6pm.. Time code 04:55 He was with his girlfriend which he’d only been dating for about a month or so. He sent us a photo of a mountain pass, we didn’t at the time know it was Franschoek Pass. Time code 05:15 That was the last communication we had with them and that was just after 6pm. (whatsapped photo that the student sent his parents of the mountain pass)

VO 8 The father, who didn’t want to be identified, heard from his son again several hours later - it would be the start of a terrifying ordeal.

UPSOUND Father: They had the boot of the car open, they had the backseats down, they’d brought snacks and that and were looking out. And a vehicle pulled up. After hitting my son, threw them in the back of the car. And they drove off.

UPSOUND Father: At around 8pm, saw there was a missed call on my phone from my son and not too long after that I also saw, his bank account is linked to my bank account, I saw a significant amount go out of his bank account. Time code 06:00 And within a few minutes of that I had a call from him to say that he had been kidnapped. And if we didn’t pay ransom that they were going to kill him and his girlfriend.

NATSOUND

UPSOUND Father: One of the kidnappers then came on the phone and were very aggressive, abusive on the phone to me. 07:31 While I was on the phone I was trying to communicate with my wife to advise her what was going on. 07:51 My daughter she managed to get through on the hotline number to police who immediately put us through to the Hawks special kidnapping unit who were phenomenal.

VO 9 He spent the next hour negotiating with the kidnappers on a ransom amount.

UPSOUND Father: There were two separate bank accounts I had to transfer funds into. After that the agreement was that they would release my son and his girlfriend, but that didn’t happen. Instead they approached her father for ransom money..

LOURENSA: Can you tell us how much money you paid them?

UPSOUND Father: It was a significant amount I’d prefer not to divulge the amount. Because the kids were recovered within ten hours the bank managed to put a stop to all payments. So the kidnappers didn’t receive any of the funds.

VO 10 The students were taken to an abandoned house, and later released on the pass.

VO 11 Three days later, just one of the three alleged kidnappers was arrested. Back in Stellenbosch, it would not be the end of the spate of abductions.

LINK Here in Krige street on the 14th of August, a 21 year old university student was walking back home when he was abducted just before midnight. He was assaulted, and thrown into a silver Toyota corolla with no number plates. Three armed men drove with him in the direction of Somerset West. Now he fought back and about 9kms away from his flat he was thrown out of the car. He started walking back, and just after one in the morning he arrived home, his clothes torn and covered in blood.

VO 12 He reported the case to police the next day, but just twelve days later received this message to say the case was closed.

VO 13 The family was too traumatised to speak to us on camera, but said they’re frustrated by the lack of police investigation.

VO 14 In an emailed response, police said the case was closed for several reasons including that the victim had not given a description of the vehicle or the suspects who kidnapped him. And there was no video footage of the incident or witnesses.

ON SCREEN: According to his statement he could not give a description of the vehicle or the suspects who kidnapped him. No video footage was available of the incident outside the pub, and he also could not remember which area the suspects dropped him off. There were also no witnesses to confirm the incident and provide more information.

LINK: With kidnapping being such a serious and prevalent crime in South Africa, we had so many questions for the Stellenbosch police station commander - like why was the August abduction case closed in only 12 days? And could all of these cases be connected? Initially, the station commander agreed to an on camera interview, but did not get the green light from province in time for our appointment. And when we arrived he had left for other engagements.

VO 15 Stellenbosch police conceded in an email, that muggings have become more prevalent, and that students are soft targets.

ON SCREEN: Stellenbosch SAPS management are concerned about street robberies that are happening frequently in the CBD area. Crime analyses show that most of the complainants are students who walk home during night hours while they are intoxicated and become easy targets of crime.

LINK: Criminals have gotten more brazen. Targetting students in even broad daylight. This wasn’t the case when I was a student here many years ago. And understandably this leaves students on edge questioning their personal security. The need for vigilance has never been greater.

VO 16 Students we spoke to all had a story to tell.

VOXPOP I’ve been sexually harassed by a car guard. I’ve been bitten by a random man on the street.
VOXPOP A friend of mine had been pickpocketed. And I tried to confront the pickpocket and he ran away and got into his car. And I tried to chase him and landed up in a very intense car accident which left me with a broken leg and rehab for a couple months.
VOXPOP I was walking down Bird street and a man jumped me and I cut the side of my leg open because he was trying to steal my phone. Luckily I got away.

VO 17 Not so lucky, were Jolene Mather and her two friends who had been on a night out earlier this year and were walking home together.

UPSOUND Jolene Mather / Student It was for a birthday celebration hence the balloon on the head. And then she had a little bit of tequila in her so she was hugging trees as one does and that was why I was actually recording the video and then that’s when I saw the car.

NATSOUND Of cellphone footage DATE 25 April 2024

VO 18 Jolene threw her phone into bushes, but her friends' phones, IDs and valuables were taken.

UPSOUND Jolene Mather / Student: He just said give me your phone or i’m going to fucking shoot you and he kept saying he had a gun. I said I don’t have my phone and they said I saw you had your phone you were recording. And then someone called them to get back into the car. They wanted this to be a quick thing. They didn’t want to draw attention to themselves.

VO 19 Students are easy targets…so, what is being done to protect them? The University of Stellenbosch declined our request for an on camera interview, but said in a statement that safety measures are reviewed continuously and that more than 200 security staff are deployed across campus.

ON SCREEN: While the University for security reasons cannot provide information on all security measures, it can be noted that some 60 inhouse staff members are employed, while more than 200 specialist security contract staff are deployed. We also make use of technology and other measures to improve safety.

UPSOUND Stephen Nelson / ABC Security 00:07 The problem in Stellenbosch, we’ve got approximately 30 000 students and they enjoy themselves like young people should do.

VO 20 Some nightclubs have excellent security, but can’t control what happens on the streets.

NATSOUND “Junior junior just watch the crowd at the back there, make sure no one is hanging around please”

VO 21 Private companies are trying to plug the security gap.

UPSOUD Stephen Nelson / ABC Security: The mothers of the students have actually they came to us and said what can we do.

NATSOUND Showing App

VO 22 Security company manager Stephen Nelson said they offer a service specifically for students - an app that allows them to make direct contact with their security control room.

UPSOUND Stephen Nelson / ABC Security: SAPS, their hands are tied, they just have so many vehicles and so many bodies that can assist during the course of the night. 00:20 When alcohol starts creeping in, people don’t think properly and they get into difficult situations. They get abducted, their possessions get stolen, their cellphones get stolen, and its just a nightmare.

VO 23 A very real nightmare that unfolded for a student outside a nightclub in a recent abduction case on the 8th of September.

UPSOUND Jodi Aigner / Mother: His friends, they were still outside the pub and saw him yanked into car.

VO 24 His mother Jodi Aigner said his friends immediately tracked his location through a tracking app, but his phone was subsequently switched off in a neighbouring township.

UPSOUND Jodi Aigner: The signal of the life 360 tracking app ended at the river. They actually thought they were going to find a body in a river.

VO 25 The abduction lasted several hours.

UPSOUND Jodi Aigner: They took all his valuables and they just left him and he had no idea where he was. A taxi stopped for him and it so happened that one of the people on the vehicle was a security officer from the Stellenbosch campus and actually said you were lucky not to be attacked further and said we’re taking you right back home.

VO 26 The victims in four of the abduction cases were too traumatised to talk to us. We chose not to approach the victim in the fifth case as the incident was still recent. The emotional impact of their ordeals likely to linger for months to come.

VO 27 For the parents, its been a wake up call that they hope no other families will have to experience.

LOURENSA: What would justice look like to you and your family?

UPSOUND Father: They need to arrest these gangs or syndicates. It’s got to be put to a stop.

UPSOUND Jolene Mather / Student It was for a birthday celebration hence the balloon on the head. And then she had a little bit of tequila in her so she was hugging trees as one does and that was why I was actually recording the video and then that’s when I saw the car. NATSOUND Of cellphone footage DATE 25 April 2024 VO 18 Jolene threw her phone into bushes, but her friends' phones, IDs and valuables were taken. UPSOUND Jolene Mather / Student: He just said give me your phone or i’m going to fucking shoot you and he kept saying he had a gun. I said I don’t have my phone and they said I saw you had your phone you were recording. And then someone called them to get back into the car. They wanted this to be a quick thing. They didn’t want to draw attention to themselves. VO 19 Students are easy targets…so, what is being done to protect them? The University of Stellenbosch declined our request for an on camera interview, but said in a statement that safety measures are reviewed continuously and that more than 200 security staff are deployed across campus. ON SCREEN: While the University for security reasons cannot provide information on all security measures, it can be noted that some 60 inhouse staff members are employed, while more than 200 specialist security contract staff are deployed. We also make use of technology and other measures to improve safety. UPSOUND Stephen Nelson / ABC Security 00:07 The problem in Stellenbosch, we’ve got approximately 30 000 students and they enjoy themselves like young people should do. VO 20 Some nightclubs have excellent security, but can’t control what happens on the streets. NATSOUND “Junior junior just watch the crowd at the back there, make sure no one is hanging around please” VO 21 Private companies are trying to plug the security gap. UPSOUD Stephen Nelson / ABC Security: The mothers of the students have actually they came to us and said what can we do. NATSOUND Showing App VO 22 Security company manager Stephen Nelson said they offer a service specifically for students - an app that allows them to make direct contact with their security control room. UPSOUND Stephen Nelson / ABC Security: SAPS, their hands are tied, they just have so many vehicles and so many bodies that can assist during the course of the night. 00:20 When alcohol starts creeping in, people don’t think properly and they get into difficult situations. They get abducted, their possessions get stolen, their cellphones get stolen, and its just a nightmare. VO 23 A very real nightmare that unfolded for a student outside a nightclub in a recent abduction case on the 8th of September. UPSOUND Jodi Aigner / Mother: His friends, they were still outside the pub and saw him yanked into car. VO 24 His mother Jodi Aigner said his friends immediately tracked his location through a tracking app, but his phone was subsequently switched off in a neighbouring township. UPSOUND Jodi Aigner: The signal of the life 360 tracking app ended at the river. They actually thought they were going to find a body in a river. VO 25 The abduction lasted several hours. UPSOUND Jodi Aigner: They took all his valuables and they just left him and he had no idea where he was. A taxi stopped for him and it so happened that one of the people on the vehicle was a security officer from the Stellenbosch campus and actually said you were lucky not to be attacked further and said we’re taking you right back home. VO 26 The victims in four of the abduction cases were too traumatised to talk to us. We chose not to approach the victim in the fifth case as the incident was still recent. The emotional impact of their ordeals likely to linger for months to come. VO 27 For the parents, its been a wake up call that they hope no other families will have to experience. LOURENSA: What would justice look like to you and your family? UPSOUND Father: They need to arrest these gangs or syndicates. It’s got to be put to a stop.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): The university town of Stellenbosch is known for it's beauty and relative safety, but an alarming crime trend has struck fear into the hearts of students living there.
metadata.Unique Selling Point: In the past four months, there have been five incidents of abductions involving students from the University of Stellenbosch. In June, a girl was abducted outside a nightclub in the early hours of the morning, and released unharmed after being driven around. In the same month, a student couple who had stopped to star gaze on the Franschoek Pass, was abducted and taken to an abandoned house where their parents were phoned and a ransom demanded. Both parents paid, and the couple was released unharmed. In August, a student was abducted and released 9kms outside of Stellenbosch, after being robbed of his cellphone and money. In a recent incident on the 8th of September, a university student was abducted outside a nightclub and driven around for several hours. He was robbed of his valuables and eventually released unharmed in Cloetesville, in the early hours of the morning. In the most recent case, on the 3rd of October, a 20 year old Stellenbosch University student was walking home in the early hours of the morning when she was abducted and held for ransom. Once her family paid, she was released the following day. The alleged kidnappers, two Zimbabwean nationals, were arrested, and face charges of kidnapping, extortion, rape and contravening the Immigration Act. They will apply for bail on the 23rd of October in the Stellenbosch Magistrate's Court.
metadata.Summary: Crime in the once relatively safe university town of Stellenbosch has spiked in recent months. Students reporting incidents of violent muggings has become a daily occurrence. On September 18th, a first year student was walking to the engineering faculty just 500 meters from his home when he was held up at gunpoint in the morning. His backpack was stolen and the two attackers fled on foot. Most concerning are the abductions. Parents of students are so concerned they have created safety WhatsApp groups and are urging students to sign up to private security companies.
